# Desktop session

The GNU root starts a Weston kiosk session as `desktop`, uid 1001, with seatd, Debian's udev daemon and PulseAudio. `init-metal` supervises `rach2-desktop`; the script starts the device services before the user session. Its output goes to `/var/log/services`.

## Use

The account has a locked password and belongs to `seat`, `video`, `render`, `input` and `audio`. Root can enter it with `su -s /bin/bash desktop`. Its private runtime directory is `/run/user/1001`, created at boot with mode 0700. Set `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1001`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0` and `PULSE_SERVER=unix:/run/user/1001/pulse/native` when starting a program there from another session.

`/etc/xdg/weston/weston.ini` selects kiosk-shell, Xwayland and no idle blanking. The session chooses headless with Pixman when no DRM connector is connected. A connected display uses DRM with Pixman, or GL when a render node exists. Weston's log in `/var/log/services` names the renderer and each output's modes, the current one marked. To set an output's resolution, add `[output]` with `name=Virtual-1` and `mode=1024x768` to `weston.ini` and restart the session with `kill -HUP $(cat /run/rach2-desktop.pid)`. When Weston ends, by a signal or by quitting, the session ends and the console takes the screen and keyboard back; SIGHUP to the supervisor starts it again. Stop the supervisor to restart the device services as well; init starts it again. Each supervisor ends and reaps its children on exit. [desktop(7)](../../../man/man7/desktop.7) gives the display's details.

## Design

`rach2-desktop` makes `/tmp/.X11-unix` and `/tmp/.ICE-unix`, mode 1777, as Debian's `tmpfiles.d/x11.conf` does at boot, since Weston's Xwayland module binds its listening socket there and Weston 14.0.2 exits with a segmentation fault when that bind fails. It starts systemd-udevd outside systemd, waits for its control socket to answer, triggers existing devices and settles their events. It starts seatd with `SEATD_VTBOUND=0` because Rach2 has no VT interface. The seat socket belongs to the `seat` group. The session starts only after that socket exists, under the desktop account's supplementary groups and a private D-Bus session bus. udevd runs with `--resolve-names=early`, so that Debian's rules give the DRM nodes the groups `video` and `render` and the event devices `input`; with `never` it would leave every node root's group. The supervisor writes its pid to `/run/rach2-desktop.pid` and runs the session as a process group of its own; SIGHUP ends that group and starts a new session, and a session that ends is not started again until SIGHUP, so that a killed Weston leaves the console its screen. A device service that ends makes the supervisor exit, so that init restarts the whole.

`rach2-session` runs PulseAudio and Weston in the foreground. PulseAudio runs `/etc/pulse/rach2.pa` alone, not Debian's `default.pa`; it loads `module-oss` over `/dev/dsp` without mmap, as the sink `oss_output` and the source `oss_input`, whose names differ since PulseAudio keeps one namespace for both, and exposes the user's native PulseAudio socket. It also loads `module-suspend-on-idle`, as PulseAudio's default configuration does: after five seconds without a client that needs a sink or source, that endpoint suspends. Once both suspend, the OSS module closes `/dev/dsp`, stopping the device's streams when no other open uses them; the next client resumes its endpoint. Without the idle module, OSS keeps writing silence and reading capture while idle. A machine without sound can still start the session. `/etc/asound.conf` gives ALSA clients a `plug` conversion over the OSS plugin. Both routes use the kernel's mixer; the ALSA default opens OSS directly. Programs that use PulseAudio find its socket through `PULSE_SERVER`.

## Building

`install_root.sh` installs the scripts and configuration after the Debian packages and locks the account the manifest supplies. The root image depends on every file here. `make ARCH=x86_64 os-real-gnu-ext2` rebuilds the image after an edit.

## Tests

The `desktop` family boots the GNU root with `rach2.audio.loopback`. Its headless case reads the compositor's uid, the seat socket, the input properties and the browser and ALSA tones recorded through OSS. It leaves the normal browser sandbox enabled. Its display cases boot the `std-vga` and `virtio-vga` profiles and run [`tests/graphics/desktop_display.py`](../../../tests/graphics/desktop_display.py): Weston's DRM output and renderer, the nodes' groups, both browsers taking keys and a click through QMP, `weston-simple-egl`, two modes through `weston.ini`, and the console's scanout and keyboard after Weston's SIGKILL; on i686, evdev, an llvmpipe render and modetest.
